messages:
Jamal: alerting — sustained p99 token latency rising in usw1 since 03:40 UTC. root cause trace points to a single tenant 'ml-prep-analytics' doing large staged batches. NIC tx queues and kvcache churn are through the roof. anyone oncall?

Ivy: I'm on. seeing host-level egress spike ~5x on a handful of hosts, and KV cache eviction rate jumped 6k/s. This is spilling into shared warm slots.

Ravi: Can we gate them quickly? options: (A) temporary egress quota + soft-quarantine (B) move them to preemptible pool with strict bandwidth shaping (C) carve a tiny dedicated slice. My vote is A+fallback to preemptible. Quicker and lower risk.

Tess: Agreed A first. Quarantine may be safer than carving — avoid rebalancing churn. Proposed rwdctl patch to apply egress policer:

```
rwdctl tenant update ml-prep-analytics --egress-limit 150mbps --soft-quarantine true --quarantine-duration 2h
```

Jamal: +1. Also enable nic-shaper on those hosts to drop extra burst, and set routing fallback to preemptible pool if they exceed soft-quarantine.

Ivy: I'll run the command and patch shaping rules on those hosts. Patching now.

ops-bot: Ticket INF-4322 created: "ml-prep-analytics egress quota + soft quarantine". Linked runbook: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/egress-soft-quarantine

Ravi: Heads up — if this keeps happening we should formalize a "burst credits" program. Tenants that need heavy batch windows sign up and get time-limited reserved capacity instead of impacting shared pools.

Tess: Patch applied. telemetry in 2m. I'll stream logs here.

Ivy: Initial numbers: p99 down ~20%, host nic tx down ~45% on impacted hosts, kv eviction rate down. Quarantine triggered for 1 host (threshold 160mbps) and traffic moved to preemptible fallback for ~3% of requests.

Jamal: Good. Keep quarantine on for 2hrs, but add a 30min cooldown and gradual drain if stable to avoid cold starts for their job.

Ravi: Filing a short RFC: burst-credits + scheduled background windows for batch workloads. Will add cost model and API surface.

Ivy: Also leaving a note for infra-sre: can we have a metric that flags cross-host kvcache regen correlation with host egress? would make root-cause triage faster.

Tess: +1 on metric. created dashboard card: "kvcache_regen_vs_egress_correlation".

ops-bot: INF-4322 updated: action items assigned to Ravi (RFC), Ivy (monitoring), Tess (dashboard), Jamal (runbook update).
